    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_16" sourceRef="Task_ExtendOffer" targetRef="Gateway_NegotiationChoice"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_NegotiationNeeded" name="Negotiation needed" sourceRef="Gateway_NegotiationChoice" targetRef="Task_NegotiateSalary">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">salary negotiation is needed</bpmn:conditionExpression>

rules.instruction: When the description states an order among process stages, describes branches that converge, or says that multiple required activities must finish before a later stage or process completion: Model the sequence flows that connect the corresponding elements, preserving the stated order and branch-and-join structure. Use gateway types that match whether the description specifies a choice or requires all branches to complete.
rules.situation: the description states an order among process stages, describes branches that converge, or says that multiple required activities must finish before a later stage or process completion

rules.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules.situation: the description states an activity or process outcome

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity may take place before a shared continuation: Model an exclusive gateway that routes either through the optional activity or around it, then rejoin the paths before the shared continuation.
rules.situation: the description states that an activity may take place before a shared continuation

rules.instruction: When the description says that a broader process stage begins and names activities included in it: Label the corresponding BPMN activity to express the start of that stage; do not label it as performing or finishing one of the included activities unless the description says so.
rules.situation: the description says that a broader process stage begins and names activities included in it

rules.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the described action as an activity after that event; do not use the start event alone to represent the action.
rules.situation: the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action

rules.instruction: When the description names components included in a broader process stage but does not specify the action performed for each component: label each corresponding activity neutrally with the stated component; do not imply that someone provides, performs, or completes it unless the description supports that action
rules.situation: the description names components included in a broader process stage but does not specify the action performed for each component
